purpose: Second directory rename: Vol.2 and Vol.3 swap places so that the reading order is NIM (Vol.1), then Nemotron on NIM (Vol.2), then Nemotron and other models as judges (Vol.3). Input of tools/renumber_dirs.py --gen 2. For every path the first rule that matches wins; the same rules move tracked, ignored and untracked files.
subject: Swap the Vol.2 and Vol.3 directories to follow the new volume order (moves only)
commit_body: vol3-nemotron/ -> vol2-nemotron/ (Vol.2, Nemotron on NIM), vol2-guardrails/ -> vol3-judges/ (Vol.3, judges in NeMo Guardrails). Both new names have never been used before.

moves.why: Vol.2: NIM + Nemotron (two deployment options, footprint, speed, concurrency, long context)
Vol.3: judges in NeMo Guardrails (the Llama judge baseline data; the judge study is to follow)

history_files_rule: Files that record past paths on purpose. The docs phase leaves them as they are; they are updated by hand in the same batch.

new.vol3-judges-baseline: Vol.3 (baseline data; the judge study has not been published)

tag_message: the last commit before the directory renames that holds this volume's runs at the paths their pre-registrations name
note_on_frozen_paths: Frozen harnesses import with the paths written at the time. They are bound by SHA-256 and are not edited, so they run as written only at the tag of their volume. PATH_MAP.md maps every old path through both renames.
path_map_intro: Directories were renamed twice: on 2026-09-28 to match the volume numbers, and on 2026-09-29, when Vol.2 and Vol.3 swapped places so that Nemotron on NIM (Vol.2) comes before the judges (Vol.3). Files written before a rename, including frozen pre-registrations, refer to the paths of their day; this file maps every one through both renames. To reproduce a run byte for byte, check out the tag listed for its volume. Check out a tag or the tip of the branch; a pure-rename commit alone is not a supported checkout (its .gitattributes still names the paths before it).
